algorithm.title: Management of Patients with Low Cardiovascular/Congestive Heart Disease (CV/CHD) Risk.

cell.label: Patients with low CV/CHD risk (6 months after MI, PCI, BMS, CABG, stroke; 12 months if associated with complications) on aspirin therapy who require surgery.
Low Surgical Hemorrhagic Risk • Peripheral/plastic/general surgery, biopsies; minor orthopedic, ENT, endoscopy; eye anterior chamber; dental (any type) • Transfusion seldom required.
Proceed with elective surgery; maintain aspirin. C
Intermediate Surgical Hemorrhagic Risk • Visceral; CV; Major orthopedic, ENT, reconstructive; endoscopic urologic • Transfusion often required.
High Surgical Hemorrhagic Risk • Possible bleeding in closed space; intracranial neurosurgery; spinal canal surgery; eye posterior chamber surgery.
Proceed with elective surgery; maintain statin; withdraw aspirin (7 or fewer days prior) and resume 24 hours after surgery. C

footnotes.footnote: Adapted from Di Minno MN, Prisco D, Ruocco AL, et al. Perioperative handling of patients on antiplatelet therapy with need for surgery. Intern Emerg Med 2009;4:279–288; updated 2022

algorithm.title: Management of Patients with Intermediate Cardiovascular/Congestive Heart Disease (CV/CHD) Risk.

cell.label: Patients with intermediate CV/CHD risk (12 months after drug-eluting stent; low ejection fraction, diabetes, high-risk stents (long, proximal, multiple, overlapping, small vessels, bifurcation) who require surgery.
Low Surgical Hemorrhagic Risk • Peripheral, plastic, general, biopsies; minor orthopedic, ENT, endoscopy; eye anterior chamber; dental (any type)/facial • Transfusion seldom required.
Proceed with elective surgery; maintain aspirin, stop P2Y12 agent: clopidogrel (5 days prior), ticagrelor (3-5 d), prasugrel (7 d); continue or stop DOAC (1d) C
Intermediate Surgical Hemorrhagic Risk • Visceral; CV; Major orthopedic, ENT, reconstructive; endoscopic urology • Transfusions often required.
Postpone elective surgery; proceed with necessary surgery; maintain aspirin, stop P2Y12 agent; stop DOAC (2 d). C
High Surgical Hemorrhagic Risk • Possible bleeding in a closed space; intracranial neurosurgery; spinal canal surgery; eye posterior chamber surgery.
Postpone elective surgery; proceed with necessary surgery; consider discontinuing aspirin; stop P2Y12 agent and DOAC. C

footnotes.footnote: Adapted from Di Minno MN, Prisco D, Ruocco AL, et al. Perioperative handling of patients on antiplatelet therapy with need for surgery. Intern Emerg Med 2009;4:279–288, updated 2022

algorithm.title: Management of Patients with High Cardiovascular/Congestive Heart Disease (CV/CHD) Risk.

cell.label: Patients with high CV/CHD risk (6 weeks after MI, PCI, BMS, CABG; 6 months after same if complications; 12 months after high-risk drug-eluting stent; 2 weeks after stroke who require surgery.
Low Surgical Hemorrhagic Risk • Peripheral, plastic, general, biopsies; minor orthopedic, ENT, endoscopy; eye anterior chamber; dental extraction and surgery • Transfusion seldom required.
Postpone elective surgery; proceed with vital or emergency surgery; maintain aspirin and clopidogrel. C
Intermediate Surgical Hemorrhagic Risk • Visceral; CV; Major orthopedic, ENT, reconstructive; endoscopic urology • Transfusion often required.
Postpone elective surgery; proceed with vital or emergency surgery; maintain aspirin and clopidogrel. C
High Surgical Hemorrhagic Risk • Possible bleeding in closed space; intracranial neurosurgery; spinal canal surgery; eye posterior chamber surgery.
Proceed only with vital or emergency surgery; maintain aspirin; bridge with tirofiban/eptifibatide (Aggrastat/Integrilin) and heparin. C

footnotes.footnote: Adapted from Di Minno MN, Prisco D, Ruocco AL, et al. Perioperative handling of patients on antiplatelet therapy with need for surgery. Intern Emerg Med 2009;4:279–288.

cell.label: Patient with required INR monitoring.
Assess need for bridging anticoagulation (high thrombotic risk) with therapeutic-dose SC LMWH or IV UFH.
Stop VKA approximately 5 days (at a minimum) before surgery to allow for INR to normalize (Grade 1B)? B
If INR remains elevated (≥1.5) 1 to 2 days prior to surgery, administer low-dose oral vitamin K (1-2 mg) to normalize INR (Grade 2C).
Resume VKAs approximately 12-24 hours after surgery when adequate hemostasis is achieved (Grade 1C).
Proceed to .

footnotes.footnote: Abbreviations: INR, international normalized ratio; SC LMWH, subcutaneous low molecular weight heparin; intravenous UFH, intravenous unfractionated heparin; VKA, vitamin K antagonists.

Adapted from Douketis JD, Berger PB, Dunn AS, et al. The perioperative management of antithrombotic therapy. American College of Chest Physicians Evidence-Based Clinical Practice Guidelines (8th Edition). Chest 2008;133(6 Suppl):299s–339s.

algorithm.title: Management of Patients with Mechanical Valves, Atrial-Fibrillation, or Venous Thromboembolism (VTE).

cell.label: For patients with mechanical heart valves, atrial fibrillation, VTE.
HIGH RISK for thromboembolism.
Bridging anticoagulation with therapeutic-dose SC LMWH or IV UFH (SC LMWH preferred over IV UFH) (Grade 1C, C ).
MODERATE RISK for thromboembolism.
Bridging anticoagulation with therapeutic-dose SC LMWH or IV UFH (SC LMWH preferred over IV UFH) or low-dose SC LMWH (Grade 2C, C ).
LOW RISK for thromboembolism.
Low-dose SC LMWH or no bridging (Grade 2C, C ).

footnotes.footnote: Abbreviations: SC LMWH, subcutaneous low molecular weight heparin; intravenous UFH, intravenous unfractionated heparin; VKA, vitamin K antagonists; VTE, venous thromboembolism.

Adapted from Douketis JD, Berger PB, Dunn AS, et al. The perioperative management of antithrombotic therapy. American College of Chest Physicians Evidence-Based Clinical Practice Guidelines (8th Edition). Chest 2008;133(6 Suppl):299s–339s.

algorithm.title: Management of Patient Taking Aspirin and/or P2Y12 Agent.

cell.label: Patient taking aspirin and/or clopidogrel.
Not at high risk of cardiac event.
Interruption of antiplatelet drugs (Grade 1C, C ).
At high risk of cardiac event (exclusive of coronary stents) scheduled for noncardiac surgery.
Continue aspirin up to and beyond time of surgery (Grade 2C, C ) Interruption of clopidogrel at least 5 days and preferably 10 days prior to surgery (Grade 2C, C ).
Scheduled for CABG.

Continue aspirin up to and beyond time of surgery and restart 6-48 hours after surgery (Grade 1C, C ) Interruption of clopidogrel at least 5 days and preferably 10 days prior to surgery (Grade 1C, C ).
Scheduled for PCI.
Continue aspirin up to and beyond time of surgery (Grade 2C) If clopidogrel is interrupted prior to PCI, recommend resuming with loading dose of 300-600 mg (Grade 2C).
Bare metal coronary stent placement within 6 weeks of surgery.
Continue aspirin and clopidogrel in the perioperative period (Grade 1C, C ).
Drug-eluting coronary stent placement within 12 months of surgery.
Continue aspirin and clopidogrel in the perioperative period (Grade 1C, C ).

footnotes.footnote: Abbreviations: CABG, coronary artery bypass graft; PCI, percutaneous intervention.

Adapted from Douketis JD, Berger PB, Dunn AS, et al. The perioperative management of antithrombotic therapy. American College of Chest Physicians Evidence-Based Clinical Practice Guidelines (8th Edition). Chest 2008;133(6 Suppl):299s–339s.
